title: Greenhouse challenge: grow more with a water budget
subtitle: Compare a fair pair, test a growing plan and revise the decision
objective: Apply plant biology to unfamiliar growth data and justify a plan using evidence and its limitations.

sow.exactOutcome: Apply plant biology to unfamiliar data.
sow.alignment: Directly develops C38 by comparing plant growth, light and supplied water. Core tasks use fair single-factor pairs and a budget decision. Interactions between limiting factors are explicitly optional Higher-tier stretch linked to Pearson 6.4; the core does not require inverse-square calculations.

priorLearning: Photosynthesis makes glucose that can contribute to plant biomass.
Water enters roots and can be lost by transpiration.
A fair comparison keeps other relevant conditions similar.
success: Choose a fair pair to investigate one variable.
Use numerical evidence to justify a plan against two stated conditions.
Explain a biological mechanism while distinguishing observed data from a guarantee.

vocabulary.meaning: Mass of living material; dry biomass excludes the water removed during drying.
Average increase across a group, not a promise for every plant.
A condition a proposed plan must meet.
A repeat experimental unit used to examine variation.
A decision in which improving one outcome may make another harder to achieve.
A factor whose availability restricts a process rate.

equipment: Printed shared evidence and one selected response route; pen, ruler and calculator.
Projector or offline HTML/PowerPoint. Optional word processor or spreadsheet.
preparation: Print the shared evidence page, one chosen response route and exit page. Routes are alternatives, not a workload ladder.
Read the teacher answers before teaching. All numerical sample data in this lesson are constructed for learning.
All tables are a constructed research scenario, not results from this school. Matched plants of the same species/age were randomly assigned; temperature, nutrients and pot size were held comparable.

Dry-biomass gain is estimated from matched groups sampled at the start and after 14 days,5 plants per group. It is not repeated destructive weighing of the same living plant. No pupil drying, heating or weighing practical is required.
For optional ICT, pupils can enter the supplied table into a spreadsheet and compare two selected columns. A paper decision brief is fully equivalent.
safety: Paper/data activity. No heating, cutting, plant infection, soil handling or electrical practical is required.
practicalAlternative: All research conditions, source summaries and constructed results are supplied. Pupils can annotate a decision chart, dictate a claim or produce a paper recommendation.

misconceptions.claim: The largest growth number always wins.
misconceptions.correction: A plan must meet all stated constraints, including the water-supply budget.
misconceptions.check: Ask whether B’s 0.60 L exceeds the 0.50 L cap.

misconceptions.claim: A mean tells us every plant grew by that amount.
misconceptions.correction: It summarises a group; individual variation is not shown by the mean alone.
misconceptions.check: Ask which extra data would show consistency.

misconceptions.correction: Some supplied water may remain in the soil, drain away or be used/retained; the table does not measure exact loss.
misconceptions.check: Ask pupils to label the water column as supplied, not transpired.

misconceptions.claim: A single successful trial guarantees future success.
misconceptions.correction: Different plants, weather, pests and sampling variation can change outcomes.
misconceptions.check: Request a repeat trial and a limitation before recommendation.

access.supported: Same core scientific goal, with word bank, short prompts, read-aloud or pointing/dictation. Do not assign a route from diagnosis.
access.standard: Use the supplied evidence to explain and justify an independent scientific decision.
access.stretch: Optional challenge after secure core: evaluate a limitation and transfer the science. Higher-tier-only material, where present, is labelled explicitly.
access.regulation: Preview the sequence. Offer solo or partner work, a pass and quiet response. Allow a brief reset and re-entry at the next numbered task; no compulsory disclosure, performance or speed competition.

slides.title: Can the best grower fail the brief?
body: Mission: recommend a growing plan with evidence.
A water budget arrives after the first decision.
slides.notes: Ask what “best” needs to mean. Keep the first choice provisional so revision is normal scientific reasoning, not a trick or public failure.

slides.title: Link plants with evidence
body: R1. How can photosynthesis contribute to biomass?
R2. Is water supplied the same as water lost?
R3. Does a group mean describe every individual?
slides.notes: R1 glucose provides material for organic molecules/biomass; light supplies energy. R2 no: water has several destinations. R3 no. Use an everyday mean example if needed.

slides.title: I check what actually changed
body: The table shows light and water supplied.
A versus B changes both.
C versus D keeps supplied water equal.
slides.notes: Think aloud: “I cannot isolate light by comparing A/B because their water totals also differ. C/D changes the intended light level with 0.15 L supplied in each; other stated conditions match.” Unequal plants could still create variation, so repeats/random assignment matter.

visual.title: A controlled comparison needs a fair pair
visual.description: Experimental-design comparison: A(low light,0.30 L), B(high light,0.60 L), C(low light,0.15 L), D(high light,0.15 L). Major conditions other than shown light/water match. C/D isolates the intended light change; A/B changes both light and total water supplied.

elements.text: A controlled comparison needs a fair pair

A: low light
Water supplied 0.30 L

B: high light
Water supplied 0.60 L

C: low light
Water supplied 0.15 L

D: high light
Water supplied 0.15 L
For a light test, compare C and D: same supplied water.

slides.title: Read the outcome and its limits
body: The outcome is mean dry-biomass gain.
Dry mass reduces the effect of differing water content.
A mean still hides individual variation.
slides.notes: Model: “B’s mean gain is 3.0 g, not 3.0 g for every plant. Matching initial/end groups estimates gain without drying the same living plant twice. This table does not directly measure instantaneous photosynthesis.”

visual.title: Constructed results: growth is not the only rule
visual.description: Constructed mean dry-biomass gains over 14 days: A 1.8 g, B 3.0 g, C 1.0 g, D 1.1 g, E 2.6 g per plant. Water supplied differs; B has largest mean gain but exceeds the 0.50 L budget. E meets gain at least 2.5 g and supplied water at most 0.50 L.

elements.text: Constructed results: growth is not the only rule

slides.title: I use two tests before recommending
body: Target: mean gain at least 2.5 g/plant.
Budget: water supplied at most 0.50 L/plant.
A plan must pass both.
slides.notes: Model an invented example F:2.8 g and 0.70 L. It passes growth but fails water; do not recommend it. Use diagram to show upper-left region. Keep E’s actual decision for collaborative revision.

visual.title: Two requirements make a decision region
visual.description: Constructed scatter plot: water supplied onx-axis and mean dry-biomass gain ony-axis. Target is at least 2.5 g gain and at most 0.50 L supplied water. The shaded upper-left region meets both. Only E of the supplied plans lies there. This is a decision aid, not a biological law.

elements.text: Two requirements make a decision region

slides.title: Round 1: choose, then test the brief
body: W1. Which A–D plan has the greatest mean gain?
Apply both targets. Does any A–D plan pass?
slides.notes: B largest 3.0 g, but 0.60 L exceeds 0.50 L. A/C/D fail 2.5 g gain. No A–D plan passes both; “none yet” is a valid evidence-based decision.

table.caption: Constructed 14-day data;5 plants per matched start/end group.

slides.title: Round 2: new evidence changes the options
body: W2. Plan E: moderate light,0.45 L supplied,2.6 g mean gain.
Does it meet both targets? Give both margins.
slides.notes: E passes. Gain margin 2.6−2.5=0.1 g; water headroom 0.50−0.45=0.05 L. The small growth margin makes individual variation/repetition relevant. This is newly supplied constructed evidence, not a guessed interpolation.

visual.title: Two requirements make a decision region
visual.description: Constructed scatter plot: water supplied onx-axis and mean dry-biomass gain ony-axis. Target is at least 2.5 g gain and at most 0.50 L supplied water. The shaded upper-left region meets both. Only E of the supplied plans lies there. This is a decision aid, not a biological law.

elements.text: Two requirements make a decision region

slides.title: Round 3: keep the recommendation honest
body: W3. “E guarantees every plant succeeds.”
Improve the recommendation and request one check.
slides.notes: Recommend E for a repeat pilot because its mean meets both stated limits in this constructed trial. Need individual values/variation, repeated trials/more plants or independent conditions; no guarantee for each plant.
slides.reveal: E meets both mean-based criteria in this constructed trial. Repeat and inspect variation before a wider recommendation.

slides.title: Which claim survives both checks?
body: Choose the claim with correct evidence and scope.
slides.notes: B correct. A ignores budget; C confuses mean/individual; D confuses variables.

options.text: B must win because 3.0 g is the largest mean.
options.feedback: B exceeds the 0.50 L water-supply budget with 0.60 L.

options.text: E meets both mean-based criteria in the supplied trial.
options.feedback: 2.6 g is at least 2.5 g and 0.45 L is at most 0.50 L; scope stays with this trial.

options.text: A mean of 2.6 g guarantees every plant gains 2.6 g.
options.feedback: A mean summarises a group; individual results may differ.

options.text: A/B isolates light because both are plants.
options.feedback: Light and water supply differ between A/B; C/D is the supplied light-only pair.

slides.title: Write a decision that can be checked
body: Choose your response route.
State a plan, evidence, mechanism and limit.
slides.notes: The independent product is a recommendation with a proposed next test. All data supplied; no online lookup required.

slides.title: Make the recommendation useful
body: Check both conditions before choosing.
Link plant biology with evidence without claiming certainty.
slides.notes: Supported S1–S4; standard M1–M4; stretch T1–T4. Label the limiting-factor interaction question optional Higher. Core pupils can succeed through fair comparisons and the two-constraint decision.

slides.title: Audience challenge: what could change your mind?
body: L1. Share your recommendation.
Audience asks for one piece of evidence that could overturn it.
slides.notes: A teacher, TA or quiet partner can ask. The pupil names evidence that could change the decision: repeated gains below the target, a water requirement above the budget, or large individual variation. Capture a genuine revision or justified confirmation.

slides.title: A scientific decision remains testable
body: “Recommend E for a repeat pilot” is a claim with a next step.
A limitation makes the decision more useful.
slides.notes: Model a concise recommendation using 2.6 g mean gain and 0.45 L supplied water, followed by a matched repeat and a check of individual variation. Do not infer an optimum light or water level beyond the tested plans.

slides.title: Use the unfamiliar evidence
body: E1. Which A–D pair changes light with the same water total?
E2. Why does B fail the budget brief?
E3. Why is E a provisional recommendation?
slides.notes: E1: C/D is the fair pair. E2: 0.60 L exceeds the 0.50 L cap. E3: the result is a trial mean; individual variation and repeatability need checking. Match the next support to the comparison, budget or claim limit.

slides.title: Next useful step
body: Fair pair • two constraints • mechanism • uncertainty.
slides.notes: Shared exit minute. Accept a marked decision table with an accurate spoken reason.

pupilPages.title: Shared evidence | Greenhouse trial
pupilPages.intro: All numerical values are constructed. Same plant species/age, pot size, nutrients and temperature; random group allocation. Dry-mass gain estimated from matched start/end groups of 5 plants after 14 days.

blocks.text: The brief: mean gain at least 2.5 g per plant, with supplied water at most 0.50 L per plant over 14 days. Supplied water is not exact transpiration. Means do not show individual variation. “Low/moderate/high” are fixed trial settings, not universal growth labels.

blocks.prompt: W1. Choose greatest gain, then apply budget. W2. Test E against both limits. W3. Request one further check.

pupilPages.title: Supported route | Check both rules
pupilPages.intro: Use the shared table. Word bank: mean; supplied; budget; photosynthesis; repeat; variation.

blocks.prompt: S1. Choose the fair light-comparison pair C/D or A/B. Explain what is held equal.
S2. Which A–D plan has greatest mean gain? Why does it fail the full brief?
S3. Test E against both limits using its two values. Calculate its water headroom.
S4. Explain how photosynthesis contributes to biomass. Add one reason a mean cannot guarantee every plant succeeds.

pupilPages.title: Standard route | Recommend a repeat pilot
pupilPages.intro: Use numerical evidence and a biological explanation.

blocks.prompt: M1. Choose a fair pair to investigate light. Explain why A/B is not a light-only comparison.
M2. Evaluate A–E against both brief conditions. Recommend a plan or none, with exact evidence.
M3. Explain how light and water relate to photosynthesis and why supplied water is not exact transpiration.
M4. Propose a repeat trial or extra evidence to test the recommendation. State what finding could change your mind.

pupilPages.title: Stretch route | Test the explanation
pupilPages.intro: Optional Higher-tier interaction challenge for T1. Constructed follow-up uses the same species/conditions: low water 0.15 L, low/high light gains 1.0/1.1 g; higher water 0.60 L, low/high light gains 1.8/3.0 g.

blocks.prompt: T1. Calculate the light-associated gain difference at each water level. Explain a possible limiting-factor interaction, without claiming the data prove the only mechanism.
T2. Each endpoint dry mass minus the matched starting-group mean gives estimated gains 2.2, 2.5, 2.6, 2.8 and 2.9 g for E. Check their mean. Does a mean at least 2.5 g mean every estimate passes?
T3. An editor ranks plans by gain divided by water supplied. Calculate this ratio for B and E. Explain why the ratio alone cannot replace both brief constraints.
T4. Suggest an improved design to test whether E’s performance repeats, controlling a specific factor and recording variation.

pupilPages.title: Exit and reflection | Evidence can revise a plan
pupilPages.intro: State the decision and its scope.

blocks.prompt: E1. Which A–D pair changes light while holding supplied water equal?
E2. Explain why B fails the full brief using a number.
E3. Why is E a provisional, mean-based recommendation?
L1. What evidence question did your audience ask? Record a revised or defended recommendation.

answers.label: Retrieval
answers.answer: R1 photosynthesis makes glucose, which provides material for organic molecules and biomass. R2 supplied water may be retained, used or lost by several routes; it is not equal to transpiration. R3 a mean summarises a group, not every individual.

answers.label: W1–W3
answers.answer: W1 B has greatest mean gain 3.0 g but uses 0.60 L, above 0.50 L. A/C/D fail the 2.5 g gain target; none of A–D passes both. W2 E passes with 2.6 g/0.45 L; gain margin 0.1 g and water headroom 0.05 L. W3 recommend a repeat pilot and inspect individual variation/repeats; no universal guarantee.

answers.label: Hinge
answers.answer: A false: budget ignored. B correct with appropriate trial scope. C false: mean is not an individual guarantee. D false: A/B differs in light and water, while C/D keeps water equal.

answers.label: S1 / M1
answers.answer: C/D: both receive 0.15 L, with low versus high light; other conditions are stated comparable. A/B changes both light and total supplied water, so cannot isolate the light effect.

answers.label: S2
answers.answer: B:3.0 g mean gain. Its 0.60 L supplied water is 0.10 L above the 0.50 L cap, so it fails the full brief.

answers.label: S3 / M2
answers.answer: A 1.8 g fails gain; B 3.0 g passes gain but 0.60 L fails water; C 1.0 g and D 1.1 g fail gain. E 2.6 g≥2.5 g and 0.45 L≤0.50 L, so choose E for a repeat pilot. Water headroom 0.05 L; this is a mean-based decision.

answers.label: S4 / M3
answers.answer: Light provides energy; carbon dioxide and water are reactants used to make glucose, which contributes material to biomass. Some supplied water remains in soil/drains/is retained or used; not all is transpired. Means hide differences among plants.

answers.label: M4
answers.answer: Repeat with randomly assigned matched groups at the same light setting, water total, nutrients, temperature and pot size; report individual values/range, not only mean. Repeated mean gain below 2.5 g, water requirement above 0.50 L or high failure variation could alter the recommendation.

answers.label: T1 optional Higher
answers.answer: At 0.15 L, high−low gain=0.1 g. At 0.60 L, high−low=1.2 g. The response to light is larger with higher water supply, consistent with water restricting response at low supply. Dry-biomass outcomes integrate several processes; data alone do not identify a unique physiological cause. This follow-up is a separate constructed balanced comparison, not a relabelling of original A.

answers.label: T2
answers.answer: Sum=13.0 g; mean=13/5=2.6 g. One estimate 2.2 g is below 2.5 g, so the mean target does not guarantee every plant passes.2.5 g meets an at-least 2.5 g condition.

answers.label: T3
answers.answer: B 3.0/0.60=5 g/L supplied; E 2.6/0.45≈5.78 g/L supplied. Ratio can summarise output per supplied volume but a plan could have a good ratio while failing absolute gain or water constraints. It is not a direct physiological water-use-efficiency measurement.

answers.label: T4
answers.answer: Use independent matched replicates, random allocation, repeated trial dates and a fixed light/water treatment; keep a named factor such as temperature/nutrients/pot size comparable and report individual variation. Do not claim one additional plant eliminates uncertainty.

answers.label: Exit and assessment
answers.answer: E1 C/D. E2 water 0.60 L exceeds 0.50 L cap. E3 only a constructed trial mean; variation and repeatability need checking. L1 accepts a specific evidence-led revision or a justified confirmation. Secure core = fair-pair logic, both constraints and appropriately limited recommendation.

teacherNotes: 40 minutes: opening 2, retrieval 3, I do 10, We do 7, hinge 3, independent 11, review 3, exit 1. Zero-minute slides share their stage time.
Choose one response route. Accept accurate speech, pointing plus explanation, annotations or writing as evidence.
A quiet review still has an audience: teacher or TA reads the pupil’s decision, asks one evidence question, and the pupil revises or confirms it.

C/D is the fair light-only pair in the original table. A/B deliberately changes both light and supplied water. The optional Higher follow-up introduces a new balanced comparison with low/high light at two fixed water supplies; do not silently change original A’s 0.30 L value.

Interactive We do has three controlled decisions: greatest mean gain, the water-cap test, and E’s follow-up results. Paper W1–W3 uses exactly the same constructed values. The diagram is a decision model, not a simulation predicting real greenhouse yields.

Dry-biomass gain is not the instantaneous rate of photosynthesis; respiration, allocation and duration contribute to the outcome. Core pupils need only connect photosynthesis with material for growth and state the evidence limit.
